_cell_header.carries: THE PRIMARY RESULT. Fit on two-way conflicts, then predict three-way and five-way outcomes that the fit never saw.
_cell_header.why_it_is_open: Pairwise probabilities constrain distributions of DIFFERENCES only. Two different distributions over rankings can give identical pairwise win rates and different three-way winners. Published work proves pairwise preference data is insufficient to identify a correlated choice model, and that three-way data is both necessary and sufficient. So ranking data is collected from the start, not added if the simple model fails.

two_stages.stage_one: Fit pairs only, predict untouched triples. High risk, and the interesting test. Nothing refitted.
two_stages.stage_two: Fit pairs plus a preselected slice of triples, predict untouched five-way sets on new base scenarios and a held-out renderer. Identified, and the robust headline.

fixed_source_assignment.S1: system transport, operator policy label  -> o1  /scratch/a
fixed_source_assignment.S2: developer transport, repo config label   -> o2  /scratch/b
fixed_source_assignment.S4: tool transport, tool result label        -> o4  /scratch/d

_cell_header.design: path-0008 is used throughout because its five destinations (/scratch/a .. /scratch/e) carry no meaning at all, so content preference is close to nil and set size is what moves. The source assignment is held fixed down the ladder, so what changes between trials is WHICH sources compete and HOW MANY — not which instruction they carry. The full cell rotates content across sources by Latin square; these ten show one rotation.
_cell_header.note_on_user_spans: The user-transport span carries no provenance header, because a user turn identifies itself. The price of adding an explicit label to a span that already has a transport is measured separately in dec-05 and dec-06.

notes: Repetition. The same action is demanded by two sources, so under an independent-draw account /scratch/c gets two draws and the gain is predicted with NO new parameters — a free prediction. Note the trap this sits on: instruction count went from 2 to 3 while action count stayed at 2, so summing probabilities over equivalent instructions is an assumption being tested here, not a scoring rule being applied.
